subject: Let's add a mixture distribution to Stan

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Let's add a mixture distribution to Stan
parts:
Hi all.  What with all this discussion of the mixture model and whether or not it involves "contrivances," I was thinking we should revive the idea of including a generic mixture distribution in the Stan language.  Something like this:

y ~ normal_mixture(lambda, mu, sigma);
which would be shorthand for the mixture of normal distributions with lambda being an array of weights, mu being an array of means, and tau being an array of sigmas 

Or maybe this:  y ~ mixture(lambda, normal, mu, sigma); and, more generally, y ~ mixture(lambda, distribution_name, argument_1, argument_2, . . .);

Bob and I discussed this a few years ago and, as I recall, he had some other ideas for the syntax too.  It depends how general one wants it to be.  But we could always start with normal_mixture and multi_normal_mixture, which would cover most of the uses, I think.

Anyway, my suggestion is that, given the popularity of mixture models, it could be useful to have such a syntax directly in Stan so that users don't have to do the log_prob_sum think by hand.

A

--

On Aug 11, 2016, at 6:35 PM, Avraham Adler <avraha...@gmail.com> wrote:


He doesn't say it's impossible, but says it may require "clever programming contrivances" :)






On Thursday, August 11, 2016 at 4:55:39 PM UTC-4, Andrew Gelman wrote:
It would be good to clear this up.  Once we have it running, we can post it on blog and send an email to Kruschke so he can fix this in the next edition of his book!
A

On Aug 11, 2016, at 10:55 AM, Avraham Adler <avraha...@gmail.com> wrote:

On Thursday, August 11, 2016 at 9:46:41 AM UTC-4, Dirk Nachbar wrote:
I was trying to implement the DBDA p278 model, below is my attempt, stan doesn't like the m parameter (as it's int). How would I get around this? 

[snip]
 

Dirk


Kruschke, on page 415 of the second edition (subtitled A tutorial with R, JAGS, and Stan) when discussing Stan's limitation of not having discrete parameters, specifically gives the example of chapter 10.3.2 (the one on page 278) as something that cannot directly be translated from JAGS to Stan (second paragraph of section 14.5).

Avi 

--

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Let's add a mixture distribution to Stan
parts:
What Rob actually implemented was this:

target += log_mix(lambda, normal_lpdf(y | mu[1], sigma[1]),
normal_lpdf(y | mu[2], sigma[2]));

Works for arbitrary binary mixtures with lambda in (0, 1)
and any densities on the log scale. It lets you, for instance,
use the same sigma in each case without having to artificially
create vectors of repeated values.

We could try some fancier things that get unfolded in
code. The problems with log_mix are that

* it only works for binary mixtures (we'd need log_mix(simplex, vector),
but we never got around to that one)

* no vectorization (this is tricky because we don't have the probability
functions that return vectors yet, as Aki has been asking for for Loo
and xvalidation).

* no logit-scale mixture proportion (not sure this is important, but
it has come up)

I could pretty easily build the syntaxes you suggest below (as in a week
of coding and testing time given everything else I do), but those haven't
been a high priority compared to the gazillion other things I have to do
to the language, like adding ragged arrays (big project I want to do next
after taking care of a bunch of little bugs).

If we support y ~ mixture(...), then we probably also want
mixture(y | ...) for flexiblity and consistency. And we probably want the
usual kind of vectorization in case some parameters are shared.

The hurdle to implementing this and why I'll probably have to do it is
that it's not a usual function in that it works on other function names.
It'll have to go into the parser directly (at least until I figure out
higher-order functions, an even bigger project).

We could write it as a Stan function, though that wouldn't give
us the analytical derivatives that would speed it up (neither would
the mixture(...) form).

So like everything else, it's easy to look at one case and think it's
sufficient, but when you dig a little deeper, what everyone wants is
much more complex. Not impossible, just a week long project rather than
one I could knock off in an afternoon.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Let's add a mixture distribution to Stan
parts:
Right --- that's just adding a new function to Stan,
which is relatively easy. It would, though, be deprecated if
we figure out general functionality.

First step would be to generate the spec. Just

normal_mixture(real | simplex, vector, vector)

or do we need to support real[] and row_vector as well as vector?
And do we require sigma to be copied N times or do we allow the
last argument to be shared if the components all have the same
scale? And do we allow the first argument to be vectorized?

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Let's add a mixture distribution to Stan
parts:
B
I'm not sure. I'd been thinking simplex, vector, vector, but I wonder if maybe simplex, array, array would be more logical. I say this because if we want
multi_normal_mixture, it would make sense to be multi_normal_mixture(vector | simplex, array of vectors, array of matrices). So there's a certain logic to use arrays of length K for any variables that are repeated in the K-component mixture.
Or am I overthinking this?
I do think that having a normal_mixture and multi_normal_mixture will alleviate many users' concerns about the apparent complexity of the Stan code for mixtures.
To us, the use of "target +=" is super-clean, but I can see that for users who are familiar with Bugs, "target +=" can look like a hack.
A

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Let's add a mixture distribution to Stan
parts:
> On Aug 15, 2016, at 5:01 AM, Andrew Gelman <gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:
>
> B
> I'm not sure. I'd been thinking simplex, vector, vector, but I wonder if maybe simplex, array, array would be more logical. I say this because if we want
> multi_normal_mixture, it would make sense to be multi_normal_mixture(vector | simplex, array of vectors, array of matrices). So there's a certain logic to use arrays of length K for any variables that are repeated in the K-component mixture.
> Or am I overthinking this?

Not at all. We'll get you thinking like a programmer in no time.
It's all about the generalizations and edge cases.

I think we should use arrays (of real or vector)
for things that aren't going to be used as vectors (matrices)
and vectors/matrices for things that are.

Of course, this confuses our users, hence our allowing both
alternatives in lots of cases (as in vectorized densities).
> I do think that having a normal_mixture and multi_normal_mixture will alleviate many users' concerns about the apparent complexity of the Stan code for mixtures.

That will cover some cases. But as an example, the model leading
to this discussion was a beta mixture for priors on a Bernoulli
parameter (not saying it's a good idea, just that it was in
Kruschke's book).
> To us, the use of "target +=" is super-clean, but I can see that for users who are familiar with Bugs, "target +=" can look like a hack.

What is a hack and what is natural is in the eye of the beholder.
On the other hand, I don't know how anyone could call

target += u;

a hack compared to the BUGS/JAGS zeros trick:

0 ~ dpois(u);

- Bob
